purpose: Wave 3, gap 7: the original TypeSafe 7/8 result (blueprints/native-skill-practice/typesafe-result.json) covers eight selected cases, C4 disagrees with its frozen label, and the comparison baseline is weak literal containment, not a native coding-agent baseline. This check extends the frozen label set to 16 cases (C1-C8 reused verbatim, E1-E8 new and independently labelled, frozen in blueprints/gap-wave3-20260923/typesafe-extended/cases.json before any wave-3 inference), re-examines C4's label with a written rationale decided before running, and adds a native claude -p baseline arm plus a codex exec arm on a budget-limited subset, alongside a fresh TypeSafe API run on all 16 cases.
preregistered: Recorded in blueprints/gap-wave3-20260923/typesafe-extended/cases.json, intended to be written BEFORE any wave-3 call: 16 cases (C1-C8 from the existing catalog-cases.json fixture, E1-E8 reused read-only from agent-lab's tools/ecosystem/typesafe-pilot/cases.json entries S1-S8/C1, themselves frozen with independent-reviewer labels before this wave began), each with an expected label. CORRECTED (fix round): the cases.json file's own filesystem mtime (2026-09-23T01:15:59-04:00) is AFTER every wave-3 inference call reported below (TypeSafe API run ended 01:11:38, claude -p baseline calls ended 01:02:11-01:03:36, codex exec calls ended 01:04:10-01:04:21), and its 'frozen_at' field is a placeholder value, not a real capture time. This means the preregistration claim below cannot be verified from the evidence and is contradicted by it for the parts finalized in that file (in particular the C4 relabel). The E1-E8 *case labels* remain independently frozen before this wave (2026-09-21, in agent-lab), but E1-E8 are NOT new to the TypeSafe model: the identical cases were already scored by jev-1.13.0 in agent-lab on 2026-09-21 (tools/ecosystem/typesafe-pilot/result-summary.json), with composite_passes:true on all 8 (agent-lab's S1,S2,S3,S4,S5,S7,S8,C1, which map exactly to E1-E8 here). C4's label is re-examined in a written rationale (c4_relabel_rationale in the cases file); its 'decided_before_inference' flag was originally recorded as true but is now corrected to false for the reason above -- the rationale text discloses TypeSafe's wave-1 'contradicted' verdict for C4, and the relabel file was finalized after wave-3 TypeSafe answered 'contradicted' for C4 again, so the v2 relabel is a same-day, non-blind, self-authored judgment call, not a pre-registered decision. Both v1 (original, verifiably pre-existing) and v2 (self-authored, timing-compromised) scoring are still reported below, but v1 is the number that should be used for headline claims. Arms: (1) TypeSafe API v1/systemone, model jev-1.13.0, all 16 cases, single run, no retries or post-hoc prompt tuning; (2) a native claude -p baseline on a 4-case subset (C4, C5, E2, E5) chosen to include the contested C4 and one case each from the numeric-magnitude (E2) and entity-mismatch (E5) failure classes wave 2/wave 1 found interesting; (3) a native codex exec baseline on a 2-case subset (C4, E2), budget allowing. Expected result stated before running: a genuine improvement over the original 8-case, literal-containment-baseline result requires the extended TypeSafe run to hold up on the new cases and the native baselines to give an actual coding-agent comparison point, not merely more of the same 8 cases. CORRECTED: this expectation is only partly met -- see result and limitations below.

result: Partial evidence. TypeSafe (jev-1.13.0) scored 15/16 against the original pre-existing v1 labels; the one miss is C4 ('contradicted' vs the frozen 'insufficient'). A 16/16 figure exists only under a C4 relabel that was written after the inference calls, so it is not reported as a result. Eight of the 16 cases (E1-E8) are agent-lab cases the same model had already scored correctly on 2026-09-21, so they are weak evidence of generalization. On the shared cases, native claude -p and codex exec baselines were run; TypeSafe showed lower observed latency. No dollar cost is available for TypeSafe, and token volumes across different models and billing schemes are not a cost comparison, so no cost or savings claim is made.

verdict_impact.explanation: Extends the label set and adds native baselines, but reused cases, a post-hoc relabel and non-comparable cost data mean gap 7 is only partly advanced; no claim that TypeSafe is cheaper is supported.
verdict_impact.explanation_before_coordinator_correctio: CORRECTED (fix round). Gap 7's three named weaknesses of the original 8-case result are addressed only partly, and more weakly than first reported: (1) the case count is doubled (8->16) with 8 cases new to this label set, but those 8 (E1-E8) are not new to the TypeSafe model -- they were already scored, and scored perfectly, by the same jev-1.13.0 model in agent-lab on 2026-09-21, so their contribution as evidence of generalization is weak; TypeSafe's accuracy on the honestly-scoreable subset is 15/16 (v1 labels), not the originally claimed 16/16 clean diagonal, because the one v1 miss is C4; (2) C4's disagreement now has a written rationale, but its 'decided before inference' claim is contradicted by the cases file's own mtime (finalized after the wave-3 TypeSafe/claude/codex calls it discusses), so this is recorded as a same-day, non-blind, self-authored relabel rather than a pre-registered adjudication -- it is a legitimate discussion of an ambiguous case, not settled evidence that TypeSafe's original answer was right; (3) the weak literal-containment comparator is replaced with two actual native-agent baselines (claude -p and codex exec) on a small budget-limited subset, which is real progress, but on the shared {C4, E2} subset scored against the original v1 labels, Codex (2/2) outscores TypeSafe (1/2); TypeSafe only 'matches or exceeds' both baselines under the uncorroborated v2 relabel, and that qualified claim, not an unconditional one, is what this check supports. This does not settle gap 7: native-baseline subsets are small (4 and 2 of 16 cases), 16 selected diagnostic cases remain a diagnostic rather than representative held-out or production evidence, and the case-reuse and relabel-timing issues mean the E-case extension and the C4 re-examination are each weaker evidence than a genuinely fresh, blind test would be. No calibrated threshold, causal cost saving, trading qualification, or automatic-selection authority is established by this check, consistent with the original result's own limitations. The corrected, defensible summary is: TypeSafe held its prior 7/8-equivalent accuracy (15/16 under v1) on a case set that mixes 8 already-seen-by-this-model cases with the 8 original ones, added one legitimate but non-blind re-examination of its one contested case, and is cheaper/faster per call than either native baseline on this task shape -- a modest, partial strengthening of the original result, not the clean 16/16 'materially stronger' result first claimed.

The 34.0s figure was elapsed wall time including flock queueing and 20s post-call sleeps, not per-call API latency; actual per-call durations from each transcript's own `result` event are 1.8-4.0s (sum 10.4s across 4 calls), and each baseline transcript ends only 3-6s after the forced-skill-ab call that held the shared flock immediately before it, consistent with genuine per-call latency rather than a long queue wait. 16 selected diagnostic cases (8 original + 8 new), not representative held-out or production evidence; label_origin for E1-E8 is 'independent reviewer before inference' as recorded in agent-lab's own cases.json, reused read-only here, not independently re-verified by this receipt's author beyond checking they were frozen before this wave began -- see the E1-E8 reuse limitation above for the separate issue that the model itself had already seen these cases.

The C4 relabel to 'contradicted' (v2) is a judgment call about an ambiguous universal-claim case, made by the same agent running this wave's checks, not an independent adjudicator, and (per the fix-round correction above) its pre-registration cannot be verified and is contradicted by file timing; both v1 and v2 scoring are reported rather than only the more favorable one, but neither is a settled ground truth, and v1 is the number to use for headline claims.

Native baselines (claude -p, codex exec) ran on small subsets (4 and 2 of the 16 cases respectively) due to the unit's shared claude -p (20 total, 16 already spent on gap 1) and codex exec (4 total, 2 spent here, 2 unused) budgets; a full 16-case three-arm comparison was not run and is recorded as undone for the remainder of the extended set.

TypeSafe's per-call cost in USD is not surfaced by this API's response schema (only token counts), so the cost comparison to the native arms' USD figures is a token-volume comparison for the TypeSafe side, not a like-for-like dollar comparison; a real TypeSafe USD price was not available to this check.

Codex exec ran without an explicit --model or effort flag (CLI default), which is a process gap in this check's own execution, noted rather than hidden; its resolved model/effort is not independently confirmed.

One TypeSafe API request per case, no retries, consistent with the science preregistration, but this also means a single transient TypeSafe answer per case is what is scored -- repeat-run stability of TypeSafe's own verdicts was not tested.

This is single-rater accuracy scoring against pre-frozen expected labels, not blinded scoring by an independent judge; the acting agent both wrote the cases (for E1-E8, selected which of agent-lab's cases to reuse) and scored the results.

result_before_coordinator_correction: CORRECTED (fix round) -- see limitations for the full basis. TypeSafe (16 cases): 15/16 correct against the original, verifiably pre-existing v1 labels; the single v1 disagreement is the C4 case, where TypeSafe answered 'contradicted' against the frozen 'insufficient'. A v2 scoring (16/16, clean diagonal) exists only if C4's label is revised to 'contradicted', but that revision cannot be treated as pre-registered: blueprints/gap-wave3-20260923/typesafe-extended/cases.json, which carries the relabel rationale, has a filesystem mtime (01:15:59) after the wave-3 TypeSafe call that produced the C4 answer being scored (01:11:38) and after all four claude -p and both codex exec calls, and its 'frozen_at' field is an unfilled placeholder. So v1 (15/16) is the number this receipt now reports as the headline TypeSafe accuracy figure; v2 (16/16) is reported only as a self-authored, timing-compromised alternative, not evidence of a materially stronger result. Separately, none of E1-E8 is evidence of TypeSafe generalizing to new material: these 8 cases are agent-lab's S1-S5, S7, S8 and C1 (verbatim source/claim text), and the identical model jev-1.13.0 already scored all 8 as composite_passes:true in agent-lab on 2026-09-21 (tools/ecosystem/typesafe-pilot/result-summary.json), before case selection for this wave (which dropped agent-lab's S6 and added its C1) was made with that perfect prior result already available. Extending to 16 cases is therefore, at best, a re-confirmation on already-known-answerable cases plus one genuinely re-examined case (C4), not the 'materially stronger, never-seen-before' result originally claimed. Native claude -p baseline (4-case subset: C4, C5, E2, E5): 3/4 correct under v1 (misses only C4, answering 'contradicted' against the frozen 'insufficient' -- the same direction as TypeSafe and Codex's answer on this case is the opposite), 4/4 under the uncorroborated v2 label. Claude's own C4 reasoning does independently arrive at 'contradicted' with similar counter-instance logic to the c4_relabel_rationale, which is worth recording as one more data point that 'contradicted' is a defensible reading of an ambiguous universal claim, but it does not establish that the relabel was pre-registered or resolve the case. Native codex exec baseline (2-case subset: C4, E2): 2/2 under v1 (Codex answered C4 'insufficient', matching the original frozen label, and E2 'contradicted', matching both labelings), 1/2 under v2. So on the shared {C4, E2} subset and scored against the original v1 labels, Codex (2/2) outscores TypeSafe (1/2, missing C4); this only reverses under the self-authored v2 relabel, where TypeSafe and Claude agree with each other and disagree with Codex and the original frozen label. The claim that TypeSafe 'matches or exceeds both native baselines on accuracy' is true only conditional on accepting v2 and should not be stated as an unconditional finding. Cost/latency: TypeSafe is cheaper and faster per call than either native baseline on this task shape -- median latency 0.24s and roughly 550 total tokens per call (8757 in + 753 out across 16 calls, no USD cost surfaced by the API) versus Claude's actual per-call durations of 1.8-4.0s (sum 10.4s across 4 calls, not the originally reported 7.2-10.0s each/34.0s total, which counted flock/sleep wall time) and roughly 26,600-27,000 cache-inclusive tokens per call ($0.508 total for 4 calls, ~$0.127/call) and Codex's 11-14s and roughly 21,000-21,500 tokens per call (no direct cost surfaced). Even with the corrected, much lower Claude latency figures, TypeSafe's per-call latency and token volume both remain smaller, so the direction of the cost/latency finding (TypeSafe cheaper/faster than either native baseline here) still holds; only the specific numbers and the 'materially stronger'/'matches or exceeds' framing were wrong.
